title: Gujarat Titans Storm to IPL Summit With 82-Run Rout of Sunrisers
excerpt: SRH bowled out for their lowest-ever IPL total of 86 as Shubman Gill's side claim fifth straight win and confirm playoff spot
body:
Gujarat Titans dismantled Sunrisers Hyderabad for 86 — their lowest total in IPL history — to register a dominant 82-run victory at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad on Monday. The win, their fifth in a row, catapulted Shubman Gill's side to the top of the IPL 2026 points table with 16 points from 12 matches and confirmed their playoff qualification.

**The Demolition:** Batting first, Gujarat posted a competitive 168-5 in 20 overs, anchored by Sai Sudharsan's fluent 61 off 44 balls and Washington Sundar's brisk 50. The total looked par on a surface offering variable bounce, but what followed was anything but competitive. Kagiso Rabada, the South African pace spearhead, struck early with 3-28, while Jason Holder's nagging accuracy yielded 3-20 to leave Sunrisers reeling at 30-5 inside the powerplay.

**A Season Transformed:** The Titans' five-match winning streak represents a remarkable turnaround for a franchise that sat in the bottom half after their opening fixtures. Gill's captaincy, once questioned, has matured visibly — his field placements and bowling rotations against SRH were textbook. The addition of Prasidh Krishna, who chipped in with a crucial wicket, has added depth to an already formidable pace attack.

For Sunrisers, the collapse was alarming. Pat Cummins' side, who entered the match with playoff aspirations of their own, now face a net run rate deficit and must win their remaining games to stay in contention. The 86 all out in 14.5 overs will haunt a batting lineup that boasts Travis Head and Heinrich Klaasen.

The IPL playoff picture is now crystallizing with two weeks remaining. Gujarat Titans lead on 16 points, followed by Rajasthan Royals on 14 and Royal Challengers Bengaluru on 14. Tonight's RCB-KKR clash in Raipur could further reshape the standings, with rain threatening to complicate matters. For the millions of diaspora cricket fans tracking the tournament across US time zones — and the growing number watching on Willow TV and JioCinema — the business end of IPL 2026 promises high drama.

**What to Watch:** Gujarat's remaining fixtures will determine whether they finish first or second, which matters for home advantage in the qualifier. Sunrisers need wins and results elsewhere to go their way.
